title: 061/062 assert $rtoi/$itor inside an analog block; Table 9-8 marks both "No" there, so a conforming compiler FAILS them
detail:
VERIFIED against ch9-system.html. Table 9-8 (Conversion System Functions) reads $itor Yes/No, $rtoi Yes/No, $signed Yes/No, $unsigned Yes/No -- second column is 'Supported in analog context'. §9.11 names the whole extension and it is two functions: 'Verilog AMS HDL extends the conversion functions defined in IEEE Std 1364-2005 Verilog HDL so that $bitstoreal and $realtobits can be used in the analog context.' 061_rtoi.va's first sentence says $rtoi is '...made legal in the analog context', which is the exact inverse of the table it cites, and then runs `CHECKI("$rtoi truncates...", $rtoi(V(p,n)), 2)` inside `analog begin`. 062_itor.va does the same for $itor. A compiler that correctly refuses them FAILS both files; a compiler that wrongly accepts PASSES.

VERIFIED VerA behavior: src/ir/lower.zig:3179 and src/backend/codegen.zig:2645/2650 lower $rtoi/$itor unconditionally; grep found NO analog-context restriction machinery anywhere in src/. So VerA accepts and the new reject fixtures need //! xfail.

The truncation semantics 061 pins (IEEE 1364 §17.8, deliberately unlike §4.2.1.1 rounding) are real but are a DIGITAL-context rule; they have no home in this suite, which compiles one flat analog device. Do not try to preserve them.

title: 15_conversion_functions.va's first and third checks call $rtoi/$itor in an analog block; only its $bitstoreal/$realtobits half is §9.11
detail:
VERIFIED. The file asserts `CHECKX("§9.11 $rtoi truncates: 3.7 -> 3, and $itor(3) -> 3.0", $itor($rtoi(V(p,n))), 3.0)` and then folds that into `x` for the third check `CHECKX(..., x, 6.7)`. Both are Table 9-8 'No' constructs. The second check, `$bitstoreal($realtobits(V(p,n))) == 3.7`, is exactly what §9.11 extends and is correct -- keep it verbatim.

This is an edit, not a rewrite: two of three checks go, the file's remaining claim (the bit-pattern round trip is the identity on 3.7, bit-exact hence CHECKX) stands on its own.

title: Eight self-labelled "NONCONFORMING ACCEPTANCE SNAPSHOT" fixtures run connectmodule-only functions in an ordinary module and assert answers
detail:
VERIFIED against ch9-system.html §9.22 paragraph 3, verbatim: 'The driver access functions described here only access drivers found in ordinary modules and not to those found in connect modules. Driver access functions can only be called from connect modules.' Table 9-19 marks $driver_count / $driver_state / $driver_strength / @(driver_update) 'No' in the analog context of a connectmodule; Table 9-20 marks $driver_delay / $driver_next_state / $driver_next_strength / $driver_type 'No' likewise. These fixtures are ordinary modules (not even connectmodules) calling them from `analog begin`. Every one opens by admitting it: 'NONCONFORMING ACCEPTANCE SNAPSHOT: these functions are connectmodule-only.'

Subsumes the literal lens's five separate over-specification reports, which all fall out with the rewrite: 111 asserts an exact -1.0 and 110/112/113/114 assert ranges (0..63, 0..7, 0-or-1, ==0) at driver_index 0 on a signal whose own driver count they prove is 0 -- and §9.22.2/§9.22.3/§9.23.1-4 all define driver_index as 'an integer value between 0 and N-1', which with N=0 is an EMPTY index space with no defined answer. 31_driver_access.va reaches that exact conclusion in its own header ('with N = 0 that range is empty, so $driver_state(p,0) and its siblings have no defined answer to write down') and then contradicts itself by summing all six into `info`.

VERIFIED VerA behavior: src/backend/codegen.zig lowers the whole family to a constant, so five of the range assertions are satisfied for free -- they discriminate nothing.

title: 108_receiver_count.va tests a function the shipped chapter marks non-normative, and its header states the opposite of Table 9-19
detail:
VERIFIED. ch9-system.html, inside §9.22.1, reads verbatim: 'Non-normative: $receiver_count is not a subclause of 9.22 in Verilog-AMS 2.4. Where a simulator provides it, $receiver_count returns an integer...'. There is no normative clause to pin.

The fixture's header is also factually wrong twice over: 'Table 9-19 is the only driver/receiver access function marked "Yes" in the analog context'. Table 9-19 lists four entries and marks ALL FOUR 'No' in the analog context, and $receiver_count is not in Table 9-19 at all. A reader who trusts this header learns the table backwards.

Deletion, not rewrite: unlike the eight in ch09-03 there is no rule left over once the nonconforming call site is removed.
expected:
Delete 108_receiver_count.va. Also delete the `$receiver_count(p)` terms from 31_driver_access.va while doing ch09-03 (`CHECKI("and no receivers", $receiver_count(p), 0)` and the `info = $driver_count(p) + $receiver_count(p)` sum).

Add one COVERAGE.md line: '$receiver_count -- non-normative in VAMS 2.4 (§9.22.1 note); intentionally untested.'

title: The directive set has no marker for "the LRM requires ACCEPTANCE and VerA rejects" -- which is 25 of ch09's 35 reject fixtures
detail:
VERIFIED in src/backend/tb.zig:125-205 (the full directive table: param, bias, sweep, wave, psweep, temp, time, analysis, reject, lrm, xfail, print) and tb.zig:198 `if (d.xfail != null and reject.items.len == 0) return error.XfailWithoutReject`. README.md:175-208 defines //! xfail as 'the LRM says the construct is an error, the fixture demands the diagnostic, and VerA does not produce it', and makes XPASS a hard FAIL.

ch09's dominant defect is the MIRROR IMAGE and the vocabulary cannot express it. VERIFIED in ch9-system.html: Table 9-10 marks all 17 $random/$arandom/$dist_*/$rdist_* names 'Supported in analog context: Yes'; Table 9-13 marks $simprobe 'Yes'; Table 9-18 marks $table_model 'Yes'. VerA refuses every one with E0801, whose explain text in src/diag_code.zig:1953 states the policy outright ('Deliberately rejected rather than stubbed'). Each fixture concedes it in its own first four lines: 'DEBT -- this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here ... so the suite stays green on it.'

A green reject fixture over a construct the LRM REQUIRES a compiler to accept is precisely the fixture a wrong compiler passes: any tool that refuses $random for any reason passes it, and a conforming tool fails it. `reject`+`xfail` writes the requirement backwards -- there is no rejection to demand.

This item is the enabler for ch09-06, ch09-07, ch09-08 and ch09-10.

title: 20 reject fixtures demand a rejection Table 9-10 forbids -- all 17 probabilistic names are analog-context "Yes"
detail:
VERIFIED by reading Table 9-10 in full out of ch9-system.html: $dist_chi_square, $dist_exponential, $dist_poisson, $dist_uniform, $dist_erlang, $dist_normal, $dist_t, $random, $arandom, $rdist_chi_square, $rdist_exponential, $rdist_poisson, $rdist_uniform, $rdist_erlang, $rdist_normal, $rdist_t -- every row is 'Yes / Yes'. §9.13's opening sentence is the same claim in prose: 'Verilog-AMS HDL extends the probabilistic distribution functions so that they are supported in the analog context.'

All 20 files carry the identical four-line DEBT header and the identical `//! reject E0801` + `//! reject $<name>` pair. The edit is mechanical and identical per file, which is why this is one item and not twenty.

Blocked on ch09-05. Also unblocks ch09-14: the §9.13.2 argument-domain rules (mean/dof/k_stage > 0, start < end, integer seed) can never be reached while E0801 fires first.

title: $simprobe and $table_model are analog-context "Yes"; three reject fixtures demand the opposite
detail:
VERIFIED. Table 9-13 marks $simprobe 'Yes' in the analog context; Table 9-18 marks $table_model 'Yes' (read directly out of ch9-system.html, the $table_model row reads 'Yes / Yes'). §9.16's opening sentence is 'Verilog-AMS HDL supports a system function that allows the probing of values within a sibling instance during simulation.'

36_simprobe_unsupported.va quotes §9.16's own error rule ('If param_name is not known, and the optional expression is not supplied, then an error is generated') and then inverts it -- it supplies the fallback expression, which is the branch §9.16 says shall NOT error, and rejects on E0801 instead. So the file rejects the one form the LRM guarantees succeeds.

Same E0801 policy, same edit as ch09-06, but a different LRM cite and one extra defect in 36, so it is its own item. Blocked on ch09-05.

title: Both type_string fixtures die on E0201 (paramset unsupported) before the rule they claim to pin is ever reached
detail:
VERIFIED. Syntax 9-8 and Syntax 9-9 both give `type_string ::= "global" | "instance"` as an optional trailing argument, and §9.13.1/§9.13.2 restrict it: type_string shall only be used from within a paramset. Both fixtures wrap the call in a `paramset`, which VerA rejects wholesale with E0201 -- so the expectation records the paramset boundary, not the type_string rule. The rule is untested in either direction: no fixture uses type_string legally inside a paramset, and none violates it outside one.

Distinct from ch09-06 because the diagnostic is E0201, not E0801, and the fix is a different construct.

title: $signed and $unsigned are Table 9-8 "No" in the analog context and appear nowhere in the tree
detail:
VERIFIED. Table 9-8 rows: `$signed Yes No` and `$unsigned Yes No`. §9.11 extends only $bitstoreal and $realtobits, so neither name is legal in an analog block. Unlike $rtoi/$itor (ch09-01) these have no fixture at all, in either direction -- so this is a create, not a rewrite.

Same xfail posture as ch09-01: VerA has no Table 9-8 context check.

title: 38's whole expectation is `//! reject NoModule` -- VerA's phase label, not an LRM rule, and the file has no //! lrm cite
detail:
VERIFIED by reading the file: it is four lines of directives over a `connectmodule` with `always @(driver_update(d))`, and its own comment says 'This reaches FastVAF's unsupported top-level connectmodule boundary first; it does not isolate driver_update parsing.' The sidecar contains the single token `NoModule`. There is no `//! lrm` line at all, so nothing in the file connects it to §9.22.4.

§9.22 makes connect modules the ONLY legal home for driver_update, so a fixture that refuses to compile a connectmodule is refusing the legal case -- the same wrongful-rejection shape as ch09-06/07, expressed against a different diagnostic. Blocked on ch09-05.

title: 21_temperature_vt.va pins $vt to rtol 1e-6 on constants the LRM does not mandate -- a compiler using Annex D.2's DEFAULT set FAILS both checks
detail:
VERIFIED by recomputing kT/q for every constant set in annex-d-stddefs.txt. The file writes `CHECKR("$vt(300.0) is k*300/q", $vt(300.0), 0.02585200, 1e-6)` and `CHECKR("bare $vt uses $temperature = 300.15 K", $vt, 0.02586492, 1e-6)`. CHECKR admits |got-want| <= rtol*(|want|+1e-30).

§9.15 says only '$vt ... returns the thermal voltage (kT/q) at the given temperature'. It mandates NO value for k or q. Annex D.2 offers FOUR sets and its `else` fallback -- taken when no `PHYSICAL_CONSTANTS_* macro is defined -- is NIST1998 (P_K 1.3806503e-23, P_Q 1.602176462e-19).

At 300.0 K, want 0.02585200, allowance 2.5852e-8:
  SPICE    0.025851241113725592  diff 7.5889e-07  FAIL
  OLD      0.025851260754174377  diff 7.3925e-07  FAIL
  NIST1998 0.025852026903638286  diff 2.6904e-08  FAIL  <- the LRM's own default, 1.04x the allowance
  NIST2010 0.025851997154882865  diff 2.8451e-09  pass
  CODATA18 0.025851999786435535  diff 2.1356e-10  pass

At 300.15 K, want 0.02586492, allowance 2.5865e-8: NIST1998 diff 3.2917e-08 FAIL (1.27x), SPICE and OLD FAIL, NIST2010/CODATA18 pass.

The written digits are CODATA-2018 truncated to seven places -- a recording of src/backend/codegen.zig:2519, not a number the LRM supplies. Its own atomic siblings 095_vt_ambient.va and 096_vt_temperature.va already do this correctly: NIST1998 literals at full precision, rtol 1e-4, with the reason written down.

Also in this file: the header cites '§9.10 environment parameters'. $vt/$temperature are §9.15 (Analog Kernel Parameter System Functions); §9.10 is Simulator Time System Functions.

title: Nine file-I/O fixtures share one filename "fixture.dat"; 052 CREATES it, so three others are order-dependent and break from the second run onward
detail:
VERIFIED on both sides. 052_fflush.va line 19 does `fd = $fopen("fixture.dat", "a")` -- Table 9-24 type 'a' is 'open for appending OR CREATE FOR WRITING'. 11_file_position_status.va:28-29, 046_fgets.va:15-17 and 047_fscanf.va:18-20 all assert `fd == 0` on that same name, and each header justifies it with 'fixture.dat does not exist next to the testbench'. Once 052 has run, it does exist, the open succeeds, fd is nonzero and all three FAIL.

VERIFIED that the working directory really is shared: tests/torture.zig:1034 spawns each testbench with `std.process.spawn(io, .{ .argv = &.{bin}, ... })` and sets no `cwd`. No fixture removes its file.

049/050/051/053/054 saw the hazard and hedged instead of fixing it -- 049 `(position == 0) || (position == -1)`, 050 `(code == 0) || (code == -1)`, 053 a CHECKEQ of `(fd == 0)` against `(code != 0)`. Each header says so outright ('Which of the two applies depends on whether fixture.dat exists in the working directory'). Those disjunctions are tautologies that no implementation can fail.

One edit fixes both groups and is the precondition for ch09-19.

046_fgets.va and 047_fscanf.va also carry a self-contradicting header sentence: 'fixture.dat exists beside the testbench, so this open MUST yield 0' -- the assertion is the missing-file case, so the sentence should read 'does not exist'.
expected:
Give every fixture its own filename, keyed to the module: 11 -> "ch09_11_position.dat", 046 -> "ch09_046_fgets.dat", 052 -> "ch09_052_fflush.dat", and so on. Nine one-line edits, no semantic change.

Then: the three fd == 0 assertions become order-independent facts, and 049/050/051/053/054 lose the excuse for their disjunctions (see ch09-19). Fix the inverted sentence in 046/047 while there.

title: E0803 (non-negative $bound_step) and E0802 ($bound_step arity) exist in VerA and NO fixture in the entire tree fires either -- two free negatives
detail:
VERIFIED twice. src/diag_code.zig:1969-1981 defines E0802 ('$bound_step takes exactly one argument', lrm 9.17.2) and E0803 ('$bound_step argument must be non-negative', lrm 9.17.2). `grep -rl 'E0802\|E0803\|E0804\|E0805' tests/fixtures/` returns NOTHING across the whole tree.

§9.17.2 backs both: the expression is a required argument, and it shall be non-negative.

These are the cheapest items in the chapter: VerA already produces the diagnostic, so they need NO //! xfail and go green on the first run. A negative that passes today is a regression guard bought for free.

title: E0804 ($discontinuity arity) and E0805 (non-constant degree) exist and are unexercised tree-wide -- two more free negatives
detail:
VERIFIED. src/diag_code.zig:1982-1999: E0804 '$discontinuity takes at most one argument' (lrm 9.17.1) and E0805 '$discontinuity argument is not a constant expression' (lrm 9.17.1), whose explain reads 'The degree is a property of the model's structure, not of the current operating point, so it must be known at compile time.' Neither appears in any fixture.

Same free-negative shape as ch09-13. The separate LRM rule that the degree is a non-negative integer constant (plus the special value -1) has no VerA check at all and would need //! xfail -- keep it out of these two files so they stay green.

title: §9.7.2: "The $stop task shall not be used within an analog initial block" -- a one-line reject with no fixture
detail:
VERIFIED verbatim in ch9-system.html §9.7.2, final sentence of the paragraph: 'A call to $stop during an accepted iteration causes simulation to be suspended at a converged time point. This task takes an optional expression argument (0, 1, or 2)... The $stop task shall not be used within an analog initial block.'

This is the sharpest positional prohibition in §9.7 and the chapter has 133 fixtures and none of it. 056_stop.va and 12_finish_stop.va both call $stop from an ordinary analog block (legal) and neither touches analog initial. §9.7.1 is deliberately the opposite for $finish -- 'If $finish is called from an analog initial block, the simulator shall exit without performing the simulation' -- so the two tasks differ here and the fixture pins exactly that asymmetry.

VerA has no such check, so this needs //! xfail.

title: §9.20 states six separate "shall be an error" rules for $analog_node_alias/$analog_port_alias; the chapter has three positives and zero negatives
detail:
VERIFIED by reading §9.20 in full. The six rules, each a distinct sentence:
  1. 'it shall be an error for it to be a bit select or part select of a vector node'
  2. 'It shall be an error for the analog_net_reference to be a port or to be involved in port connections.'
  3. 'The hierarchical_reference_string shall be a constant string value (string literal or string parameter)'
  4. 'It shall be an error for the hierarchical_reference_string to reference a node that is used as an analog_net_reference in another $analog_node_alias or $analog_port_alias() system function call.'
  5. 'It shall be an error for the $analog_node_alias() and $analog_port_alias() system functions to be used outside the analog initial block.'
  6. 'shall not be used inside conditional (if, case, or ?:) statements unless the conditional expression controlling the statement consists of terms which can not change during the course of a simulation'

The three existing fixtures (30_node_alias_calls.va, 105, 106) are all positives on the return-0 branch. KEEP them -- contrary to the weak lens's reading, 30 is not merely a restatement of an integer default: its second check biases the un-aliased local node and reads 0.4 V back through V(), which a compiler that folded the net onto a hierarchical node would fail.

All six need //! xfail; VerA lowers both alias functions to a constant 0.0 (src/backend/codegen.zig:2607) with no structural checking.

The missing POSITIVE -- a successful alias returning 1, sharing the matrix position, and letting I(<n>) measure the aliased port's flow -- needs an instance hierarchy and is not expressible here; see ch09-27.

title: §9.15: an unknown $simparam name with no fallback expression "is an error" -- untested; 22_simparam.va covers only the fallback branch
detail:
VERIFIED verbatim in §9.15: 'If param_name is known, its value is returned. If param_name is not known, and the optional expression is not supplied, then an error is generated. If the optional expression is supplied, its value is returned if param_name is not known and no error is generated.'

22_simparam.va tests the third sentence and says so ('the one value this function pins without consulting some PARTICULAR simulator's parameter set is the fallback for a name no simulator can know'). It is correct and should be kept. The second sentence -- the error branch -- has no fixture, and it is the half a naive implementation gets wrong by silently returning 0.0.

Also: 22_simparam.va's header cites '§9.10'. $simparam is §9.15.

title: $realtime, $time and $stime are Table 9-7 "No" in the analog context, and §9.10 deprecates $realtime there by name
detail:
VERIFIED. Table 9-7 rows read `$realtime Yes No`, `$time Yes No`, `$stime Yes No`, and `$abstime Yes Yes`. §9.10 adds a note the other three do not get: 'NOTE -- In previous versions of the Verilog-AMS LRM, $realtime was supported in the analog context and it had an additional argument. This version of the LRM deprecates using $realtime in the analog context.'

14_abstime.va covers the one function that IS legal ($abstime) and is correct -- keep it. The three that are not have no fixture, and $realtime is the one a model author is most likely to reach for out of digital habit, which is exactly why the LRM bothered with the note.

Ranked above the rest of the Table 9-x sweep (ch09-19) because §9.10 states the rule twice, in a table and in prose.

title: Every file-position and status rule is pinned only on a FAILED open, so six fixtures assert tautologies -- no fixture in the chapter ever writes a file and reads it back
detail:
VERIFIED by reading all six. Each opens `fixture.dat` for reading, gets fd == 0 (or might not -- see ch09-12), and then relaxes: 049 `(position == 0) || (position == -1)`, 050 `(code == 0) || (code == -1)`, 051 a CHECKEQ of $rewind against $fseek(fd,0,0) with both sides erroring, 053 a CHECKEQ of `(fd == 0)` against `(code != 0)`, 054 `code == 0` on a descriptor nothing has read from, 046 `code == 0` for 'a failed $fgets'.

Every one of those is satisfied by an implementation that returns -1 unconditionally, or 0 unconditionally. The LRM values that go unclaimed are all exact:
  §9.5.5  $ftell returns the byte offset; $fseek and $rewind return 0 on success and -1 on error
  §9.5.4.1 $fgets returns the CHARACTER COUNT and transfers the newline into the string
  §9.5.7  after a successful operation $ferror returns 0 and leaves its string argument EMPTY
  §9.5.8  $feof returns NONZERO once a read has hit EOF

Strictly blocked on ch09-12: with per-fixture filenames each of these can create its own file with a known byte count and then assert the exact number.
expected:
One shape, per fixture: $fopen(own_name, "w"), write a known string, $fclose, $fopen(own_name, "r"), then assert the exact value.

With "abc\n" (4 bytes) written:
  049: $ftell after open == 0; after one $fgets == 4
  050: $fseek(fd,0,2) == 0 and the following $ftell == 4
  051: $rewind(fd) == 0 and the following $ftell == 0
  046: $fgets(s,fd) == 4, and s contains the newline
  053: $ferror(fd,s) == 0 and s is the empty string
  054: $feof(fd) == 0 before the read, NONZERO after the read that hits EOF

Delete every disjunction. Six exact integers replace six tautologies.

title: §9.13.2's two flat argument-domain errors have no fixture; three DEBT headers quote the rules and none violates them
detail:
VERIFIED verbatim in §9.13.2: 'For the $rdist_exponential, $rdist_poisson, $rdist_chi_square, $rdist_t, and $rdist_erlang functions, the arguments mean, degree_of_freedom, and k_stage shall be greater than zero (0). Otherwise an error shall be reported.' and 'In $rdist_uniform, the start and end arguments are real inputs which bound the values returned. The start value shall be smaller than the end value.'

Both are 'shall'-level and both are stated flatly, with no implementation latitude. 32_random_unsupported.va, 35_real_distribution_unsupported.va and 119_dist_uniform_unsupported.va each QUOTE one of these rules in their DEBT preamble and then pass legal arguments, so the rules are cited and never exercised.

DEPENDENCY: strictly blocked on ch09-06. While E0801 fires on the function name, no argument ever reaches a domain check, so these fixtures would pass for the wrong reason.

title: The remaining analog-context "No" columns -- b/h/o display variants, twelve file-I/O spellings, timescale, PLA and stochastic-queue tasks -- have no reject fixture anywhere
detail:
VERIFIED against Tables 9-1, 9-2, 9-3, 9-5 and 9-6, and against the two flat prose sentences that back them: §9.8 'Verilog AMS HDL does not extend the PLA modeling tasks defined in IEEE Std 1364 Verilog' and §9.9 'Verilog AMS HDL does not extend the stochastic analysis tasks defined in IEEE Std 1364 Verilog.' Those two are as unambiguous as the chapter gets.

This is the chapter's single largest structural hole -- 133 fixtures and not one rejects a digital-only task in an analog block -- but it is ranked below ch09-01/09/18 because those names are the ones a model author actually reaches for, and because all of these need //! xfail anyway (VerA has no context machinery at all: grep across src/ found no analog-context restriction for any ch9 system task).

Three files rather than forty: one representative per table is enough to pin the RULE. A per-name sweep is a COVERAGE.md matrix, not forty fixtures.

title: §9.21 states its own exact oracle -- f(3.5, 0.25) = 2.0 on the LRM's 12-row sample set -- and no fixture computes it
detail:
VERIFIED and independently recomputed. Figure 9-2's caption in ch9-system.html reads: 'the same isolines with a lookup at x1=3.5; the isolines yh and yl bracketing y1=0.25 are interpolated at x1, producing intermediate points which are then interpolated in y to yield f(x1,y1)=2.0.'

§9.21.5 prints the full 12-row sample set as an array-source example (y[0:11], x[0:11], f_xy[0:11] initialized inside @(initial_step)). Recomputing by hand with the default linear/linear control string:
  y=0.0 isoline at x=3.5: between (3.0,1.5) and (4.0,2.0) -> 1.75
  y=0.5 isoline at x=3.5: between (3.0,2.0) and (5.0,3.0) -> 2.25
  interpolate in y at 0.25 between 1.75 and 2.25          -> 2.0  exactly

So the LRM supplies the data, the query point and the answer, and 2.0 is exact in binary floating point. This is the single highest-value uncovered number in the chapter, and today §9.21 is represented only by two reject fixtures that pin VerA's E0801 (see ch09-07).

Blocked on ch09-05: the file will be //! xreject until VerA implements $table_model.

title: $limit's third form -- a user-defined analog function as the limiter -- is absent from the entire tree
detail:
VERIFIED. Syntax 9-12 gives three alternatives:
    $limit ( access_function_reference )
  | $limit ( access_function_reference , string , arg_list )
  | $limit ( access_function_reference , analog_function_identifier , arg_list )

26_limit.va covers the first and 27_limit_named.va covers the second (the "pnjlim" string form). The third has no fixture and is the only one that involves user code -- and §9.17.3 adds a rule that exists nowhere else: 'The arguments of the user-defined function shall all be declared input.'

So one file buys a positive (the third grammatical form compiles and the limiter is the identity below its threshold) and sets up a negative (a limiter with a non-input argument).

Both existing fixtures are sound and stay: 27's reasoning that pnjlim is the identity below vcrit -- the guard is a conjunction, bias 0.3 V against vcrit 0.7 V -- is correct and iteration-independent.

title: $simparam("timeUnit") and $simparam("timePrecision") are the only Table 9-27 names with values the source itself fixes -- and neither is tested
detail:
VERIFIED. Table 9-27 defines "timeUnit" as 'Time unit as specified in `timescale, in seconds' and "timePrecision" as 'Time precision as specified in `timescale, in seconds', both with units 's'. §9.15 adds '$simparam() shall always return a real value; simulation parameters that have integer values shall be coerced to real.'

Every other Table 9-27 name (gmin, gdev, imax, scale, shrink, tnom...) is a simulator preference with no LRM-fixed value -- 22_simparam.va says exactly this and correctly declines to assert them. These two are different: `timescale is a source directive, so the answer is derivable from the fixture's own text with no reference to any simulator's defaults.

Under `timescale 1ns/1ps the answers are 1e-9 and 1e-12, both exactly representable and both exact in double.

title: The one-argument $fopen returns a MULTICHANNEL descriptor -- bit 31 cleared, exactly one bit set -- and no fixture uses that form
detail:
VERIFIED in §9.5.1. The chapter defines two distinct return shapes and the suite only tests one. 07_file_open_close.va and 052_fflush.va both use the two-argument form and correctly assert `(fd & 2147483648) != 0` (bit 31 set = file descriptor). The one-argument form `$fopen("name")` returns an mcd instead: bit 31 CLEARED, and exactly one of bits 0..30 set. Bit 0 is standard output, so mcds OR together to fan one $fdisplay out to several channels -- and §9.5.1 makes file descriptors the opposite: 'file descriptors cannot be combined via bitwise OR'.

Also uncovered and cheap in the same file: STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR are pre-opened at 0x80000000/1/2, and '$fopen shall reuse a channel that has been closed' (07's header already quotes this sentence and does not test it).

All of it is bit arithmetic on the return value -- no file content needed, so it is independent of ch09-12.

title: 16_plusargs.va routes the destination and the return of $value$plusargs through one variable, discarding the half of the rule §9.12 exists to fix
detail:
VERIFIED by reading the file: `value = $value$plusargs("gain=%d", value);` -- `value` is both the second argument and the assignment target. IEEE 1364-2005 §17.10, which §9.12 carries into the analog context unchanged, states two things about the no-match case: the function RETURNS zero, and it LEAVES THE DESTINATION VARIABLE UNCHANGED. With one variable the second claim is unobservable -- and it is the half a naive implementation gets wrong, by zeroing or by leaving the destination uninitialized.

The file's own header states the rule correctly ('in that case leaves the destination variable untouched') and then does not test it. Two-line fix.

The $test$plusargs half is correct and stays: the header's reasoning that torture.zig spawns with `argv = &.{bin}` and therefore no plusarg is present is verified true (tests/torture.zig:1034).

title: $param_given is tested only in the "1" direction; the zero direction is one file and passes today
detail:
VERIFIED, AND THE LENS'S STATED REASON IS WRONG -- see below. 103_param_given.va uses `//! param gain = 2.0` against a default of 1.0 and asserts 1. 29_binding_detection.va does the same. `$param_given(...) == 0` appears nowhere in the tree. The weak lens claimed 2.0-vs-1.0 was chosen because it is 'the one input on which VerA's known-wrong value-comparison agrees with the correct rule'. That premise is FALSE and I dropped it: src/backend/tb.zig:321-328 emits `if (comptime @hasField(D.Model, "

__given")) @field(model, "

__given") = true;` once per //! param line, and src/backend/codegen.zig:2593 answers $param_given from that flag. It is not a value comparison. An override that EQUALS the default therefore reads as given -- correctly. Both directions are right today. So what survives is a plain coverage gap, and a cheap one: omit the //! param line and $param_given must be 0. It will PASS on the first run, which makes it a regression guard rather than a debt marker. Worth a second file asserting the override-equals-default case (//! param gain = 1.0 against a default of 1.0, still 1) -- that is the case a value-comparing implementation gets wrong, and pinning it stops anyone from 'optimizing' the flag away.

title: The display format vocabulary -- %c, %b, %r, the \ddd octal escape, the null argument, and the argument-pairing rule -- is largely unexercised
detail:
VERIFIED that the rules exist and are normative: Table 9-21 gives the escape sequences including '\ddd -- a character specified by 1 to 3 octal digits'; Table 9-22 gives the format specifications (%c one ASCII character from an integer, %b binary, %o octal, %h hex, %s, %m, %%); Table 9-23 gives the real formats including %r, engineering notation using the §2.6.2 scale factors. §9.4.1/§9.4.3 add the pairing rule: 'For each % character ... a corresponding expression argument shall be supplied after the string', with %m, %% and %l the stated exceptions that consume none.

06_display_formats.va exists but does not reach %c, %b, the octal escape or the null-argument case; 03_display_write.va does not reach %r.

Two files rather than eight: the positives collapse into one transcript, and the pairing violation is a separate negative. Ranked here rather than higher because the display transcript is already the suite's richest area and these are increments to it, not holes in the middle of it.

title: §9.5.4.2's conversion-specification rules -- %*d suppression, the maximum field width, the optional sign, and %s/%f/%g -- are unexercised
detail:
VERIFIED in §9.5.4.2: a conversion specification is 'the character %, an optional assignment-suppressing character *, a decimal digit string that specifies an optional numerical maximum field width, and a conversion code'; 'the result is placed in the variable specified in the corresponding argument UNLESS assignment suppression was indicated'; and the return is 'the number of successfully matched and assigned input items ... this number can be 0 in the event of an early matching failure'.

So a suppressed field consumes input, consumes NO argument, and is NOT counted in the return -- three separate claims in one specifier, and none of them is tested. 048_sscanf.va and 047_fscanf.va reach only plain %d.

$sscanf reads a string literal and needs no file, so unlike ch09-19 it is independent of ch09-12 and can be written immediately.

title: §3.4.7 prints `aliasparam m = $mfactor;` as its own example and no fixture makes a hierarchical parameter function an aliasparam target
detail:
VERIFIED in ch3-datatypes.html:536, which gives literally `aliasparam m = $mfactor;` in the aliasparam_declaration examples (alongside `aliasparam trise = dtemp;`). I checked this one specifically because the claim looked wrong -- $mfactor is a system function, not a parameter -- and the LRM prints it anyway, so the rule holds.

28_hierarchical_parameters.va covers the Table 9-29 top-level defaults ($mfactor 1.0, $xposition/$yposition 0.0, $angle 0, $hflip/$vflip +1) and is correct; it does not touch aliasparam. check.vh's CHECKEQ is the sanctioned form for 'an aliasparam must name the same storage as the parameter it aliases' -- its own doc comment names that exact case.

Minor, found in passing: 28's header cites '§9.16 Table 9-29'. Table 9-29 is §9.18; §9.16 is the dynamic simulation probe.

title: Two rules are not expressible in this harness and should be recorded as such rather than written as fixtures
detail:
VERIFIED that both are blocked by construction, not by effort -- which is why they are a COVERAGE.md row and not two .va files. An author who takes them from the uncovered lens at face value writes two fixtures that cannot work.

1. $port_connected == 0 (§9.19). src/backend/codegen.zig:2601 returns a hard `@as(i64, 1)` with the comment 'Every port of an elaborated device instance is connected; an unconnected one is the host's business (§6.5.6)'. Independently, src/backend/tb.zig has no directive for leaving a port unbound -- the full set is param, bias, sweep, wave, psweep, temp, time, analysis, reject, lrm, xfail, print. So the zero direction cannot be produced from a fixture at all. 104_port_connected.va tests the 1 direction and is correct.

2. Table 9-29's hierarchical COMBINATION rules (§9.18). The resolved value of an instance is the top-level value combined with what each level down specified; VerA elaborates ONE flat module, so there is no level down. 28_hierarchical_parameters.va pins the top-level defaults, which is everything the harness can reach.

Contrast with ch09-27, which the same lens reported the same way and which IS writable -- the difference is that $param_given is answered from a per-//!-param flag while $port_connected is a constant.
expected:
Two COVERAGE.md lines under a 'Not expressible in this harness' heading, each naming the blocker:
  - §9.19 $port_connected == 0 -- codegen.zig:2601 returns constant 1 and no //! directive can leave a port unbound.
  - §9.18 Table 9-29 hierarchical combination -- requires an instance tree; VerA elaborates one flat module.

Recording the blocker is the deliverable: it stops the next audit from re-filing them as fixture work.

title: 26 dead .expected-error.txt sidecars sit beside ch09's reject fixtures; the runner that read them is gone and README.md line 3 says "No sidecar files"
detail:
VERIFIED, with the lens's count corrected. `ls tests/fixtures/ch09_system_tasks/*.expected-error.txt | wc -l` gives 26, not the 35 the weak lens reported (35 is the count of REJECT fixtures in the chapter, not of sidecars). Tree-wide there are 301.

VERIFIED that they are genuinely dead, which the lens asserted without checking: the only reader is tests/conformance.zig, and grep through build.zig shows conformance is not wired into any build step -- build.zig:67-69 says 'The torture suite -- the ONE oracle over tests/fixtures/**/*.va ... It replaced conformance, exhaustive, sema.sh and ledger'. tests/torture.zig never opens them. tests/fixtures/README.md:3 states the contract: '859 .va files. One runner, tests/torture.zig. No sidecar files.'

Every sidecar duplicates the `//! reject` lines already in its .va, so deleting them loses nothing. Low severity but zero risk, and it removes a second, silently-diverging copy of every expectation.
expected:
Delete the 26 files. The `//! reject` directives in each .va are the live expectation and already carry the same substrings.

Do the other 275 tree-wide as one separate chore, not as part of ch09.

title: COVERAGE.md lists five .va files that do not exist and counts rules as covered in vocabulary the new contract bans
detail:
VERIFIED. COVERAGE.md lines 140-144 and 255-259 both list `126_rdist_exponential_lowering.va`, `127_rdist_poisson_lowering.va`, `128_rdist_chi_square_lowering.va`, `129_rdist_t_lowering.va`, `130_rdist_erlang_lowering.va`. None exists -- `ls *lowering*` in the directory matches nothing. The files that DO exist at those numbers are the `_unsupported.va` rejects, so the inventory is one rename behind.

The same document counts the 25 wrongful-rejection fixtures of ch09-06/07 as coverage, which is the accounting error that let 133 fixtures accumulate with zero conformance negatives. It is the last item because it is a consequence of ch09-05 through ch09-10 and should be rewritten once, after them, rather than twice.
expected: Delete the ten phantom rows. After ch09-05..ch09-10 land, regenerate the inventory from the directory rather than maintaining it by hand, and split the totals three ways: covered / xfail (VerA under-rejects) / xreject (VerA over-rejects). A single 'covered' number cannot distinguish the three and is what hid this chapter's defect.

title: 095/096 pick the right tolerance for the right reason but miscount the Annex D.2 constant sets as five
detail:
VERIFIED. Both headers say 'the five sets D.2 offers (SPICE, OLD, NIST1998/2010/2018)'. annex-d-stddefs.txt defines FOUR: P_*_SPICE, P_*_OLD, P_*_NIST1998, P_*_NIST2010 (lines 391-411), selected by `PHYSICAL_CONSTANTS_SPICE / _OLD / _NIST2010 with NIST1998 as the `else fallback (lines 417-455). There is no NIST2018 set in the standard header -- CODATA-2018 is what VerA's own codegen.zig:2519 uses, which is precisely the confusion that produced the ch09-11 defect in the sibling file.

Everything else in these two files is correct and they are the model ch09-11 should copy: full-precision NIST1998 literals, rtol 1e-4, and the reason written down.

The literal lens also flagged 096's `CHECKEQ($vt(600.0), 2.0*$vt(300.0), 1e-15)` as avoidable. I dropped that: check.vh's own doc comment sanctions CHECKEQ 'for the rules the LRM states as an identity with no value to write down', and linearity in T is exactly that -- writing a literal would re-import the constant-set dependency these files were built to avoid.
expected: Change 'the five sets D.2 offers (SPICE, OLD, NIST1998/2010/2018)' to 'the four sets D.2 offers (SPICE, OLD, NIST1998, NIST2010)' in both headers, and recheck the quoted 3.1e-5 max spread against four sets. No code change; the literals and the tolerance are right.
